title: Reading history fast
summary: log --oneline --graph --all, ranges, old versions of a file, which branches contain a commit, and checking out a teammate's branch for review.

steps.title: The one history view to remember
body: Before a merge, a rebase or a review, look at the whole picture:
```bash
git log --oneline --graph --all
```text
* 5c1e2f0 (HEAD -> main, origin/main) Round half away from zero
* 8d0b7a3 (tag: v3.2.0) Document the orders API
| * 41aa9c2 (origin/release/3.1) Start the 3.1 changelog
* 2f7e611 Round the cart total
| * c90d1b4 (origin/priya/free-shipping) Explain the shipping threshold
| * 7b3e0aa Free shipping over 50
* 1a2b3c4 Add orders
- `--graph` draws the lines, `--all` shows every branch and tag (not only HEAD), and the names in brackets are the decorations (on by default in a terminal).
- Add `--since=2.weeks`, `--author=Priya`, `-- src/Cart.cs` (only commits touching a path) or `-n 20` to narrow it.
- Many people keep an alias: `git config --global alias.lg "log --oneline --graph --all"`.

steps.prompt: Match the option to what it does to `git log`.
pairs: draw how branches fork and join
include every branch, tag and remote-tracking ref
follow only the main line through merges
show the diff of each commit, for one file only
list changed files with line counts

steps.prompt: You are reviewing `feature/search`. Which command lists exactly the commits a merge into `main` would bring in?
steps.explain: `A..B` is "in B but not in A". Three dots, `A...B`, is the symmetric difference: commits on either side since they forked. For diffs it is the other way round in practice: `git diff main...feature` shows what the branch changed since the fork, which is what a pull request shows.

steps.title: Look without moving
body: You rarely need to check out an old commit to answer a question about it:
```bash
git show v3.2.0:src/Cart.cs          # a file as it was at a tag (any commit works)
git show --stat HEAD~2               # what one commit changed, files only
git diff --word-diff v3.2.0 -- docs  # changes inside lines, good for prose
git branch -r --contains 2f7e611     # which server branches have this commit?
git shortlog -sn v3.1.0..            # who committed since the last release

To review a teammate's branch, check it out under the same name. `git switch priya/free-shipping` finds `origin/priya/free-shipping`, creates a local branch and sets it to track the remote one. The long form is `git switch -c priya/free-shipping --track origin/priya/free-shipping`, and `git switch -c review origin/priya/free-shipping` gives it a name of your own.

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: print `src/Cart.cs` as it was at tag `v3.2.0`, then list the remote branches that contain commit `2f7e611`.
Does the command only read, or does it change your repository?

steps.title: Answer questions from history
prompt: `~/shop` is a fresh clone of the team repo. Start with `git log --oneline --graph --all`, then:
1. Save `src/Cart.cs` **as it was at tag `v3.2.0`** in `~/answers/cart-at-3.2.0.cs`.
2. Save the names of the **remote** branches that contain the commit `Round the cart total`, one per line, in `~/answers/contains.txt`.
3. Check out Priya's branch `priya/free-shipping` locally for review, tracking the server's branch.

checks.name: cart-at-3.2.0.cs is the tagged version
checks.fail: `~/answers/cart-at-3.2.0.cs` should be exactly `git show v3.2.0:src/Cart.cs` (it has no `MidpointRounding` yet).

checks.name: contains.txt lists the right remote branches
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && diff <(sed 's/^[* ]*//; /->/d; /^$/d' ~/answers/contains.txt | sort) <(git branch -r --contains "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/round)" | sed 's/^[* ]*//; /->/d' | sort)
checks.fail: `~/answers/contains.txt` should list `origin/main` and `origin/release/3.1`: `git branch -r --contains <hash>` (find the hash with `git log --oneline --all --grep 'Round the cart'`).

checks.name: priya/free-shipping is checked out and tracks the server
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git branch --show-current)" = priya/free-shipping && test "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref '@{upstream}')" = origin/priya/free-shipping
checks.fail: You should be on a local `priya/free-shipping` whose upstream is `origin/priya/free-shipping`. `git switch priya/free-shipping` sets that up.

hints: `git log --oneline --all --grep 'Round the cart'` gives the hash; `git branch -r --contains <hash> > ~/answers/contains.txt`.
`git switch priya/free-shipping` (no `-c`): Git finds the remote branch of that name and tracks it.
solution: git branch -r --contains "$(git log --format=%h --all --grep 'Round the cart total' -1)" > ~/answers/contains.txt
steps.explain: `--contains` answers the question support asks every week: "is the fix in the release?". `git tag --contains <hash>` gives the first release that shipped it. Checking out a remote branch by its plain name only works when exactly one remote has a branch of that name; with a fork and an upstream you write `git switch -c name --track upstream/name`.
